sections.heading: Is Tickmill Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
At $6 per standard lot round-turn on raw spreads starting from 0.0 pips, Tickmill is mathematically the cheapest FCA-regulated ECN broker available to retail traders. That is not marketing — it is arithmetic. IC Markets charges $7, Pepperstone charges $7, FxPro charges $7. Tickmill charges $6. For a trader executing 100 lots per month, that is $100 saved annually on commission alone.

The trade-off is scope. Tickmill offers approximately 200 tradable instruments — almost exclusively forex, metals, and a handful of indices and bonds. If you want shares, crypto CFDs, or extensive commodity coverage, this is not your broker. But if you trade EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and gold — and you trade them frequently enough for per-lot cost to matter — Tickmill delivers the best value under legitimate regulation.

FCA authorisation (717270) and CySEC licence provide Tier-1 oversight with FSCS/ICF compensation. No inactivity fee is a genuine bonus. The execution infrastructure runs sub-20ms. And the absence of gimmicks — no copy trading, no proprietary platform, no flashy app — tells you exactly who this broker is built for: traders who already know what they are doing and just want the cheapest clean execution available.

sections.heading: Is Tickmill Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
Yes. Tickmill UK Ltd is authorised by the FCA (registration 717270) with FSCS coverage up to GBP 85,000. Tickmill Europe Ltd holds CySEC licence 278/15 with ICF coverage up to EUR 20,000. Tickmill Ltd (Seychelles, FSA SD008) serves international clients with up to 1:500 leverage but no compensation scheme. Tickmill South Africa is FSCA-regulated (FSP 49464).

Fund segregation applies across all entities. Negative balance protection is available on all account types. Tickmill does not appear on any active FCA, CySEC, or IOSCO warning list. No major regulatory enforcement actions have been recorded. NAFT last reviewed Tickmill regulation in May 2026.

sections.heading: Tickmill Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
Two account types with a massive cost difference. The Raw account: 0.0 pips average EUR/USD + $3 per side ($6 round-turn). That is the cheapest regulated ECN commission available — $1 less per lot than IC Markets, Pepperstone, or FxPro. The Classic account: 1.6 pips average EUR/USD, zero commission — costing approximately $16 per lot. The Classic exists but makes no economic sense for anyone trading more than once per week.

No inactivity fee — genuinely unusual for a regulated broker. Overnight swaps apply to positions held past rollover. No deposit or withdrawal fees on most methods. The VIP account offers $4 round-turn commission for clients depositing $50,000+ or trading 100+ lots per month.

Tickmill holds a strong Trustpilot rating of approximately 4.0 stars. Withdrawal speed is one of the most consistently praised aspects — same-day e-wallet processing is genuine and reliable.

sections.heading: Tickmill Final Verdict — Is It Worth It in 2026?
sections.body:
NAFT scores Tickmill 7.6 out of 10. The Raw account at $6 round-turn commission is objectively the cheapest regulated ECN available — cheaper than IC Markets, Pepperstone, or FxPro by $1 per lot. FCA and CySEC regulation provide Tier-1 oversight. No inactivity fee is a genuine differentiator.

The limitations are clear: only 200 instruments, no cTrader, no copy trading, minimal education. These are not weaknesses for the trader Tickmill targets — they are irrelevant. If you trade forex, trade it frequently, and measure your edge in fractions of a pip, the $1 per lot saving over competitors compounds into real money.

NAFT recommends Tickmill for the pure forex scalper who wants minimum regulated cost. If you need multi-asset diversity, look at IC Markets or FxPro. If you want education, go to AvaTrade.
